main_text.l: Lugubris pandit cum sæuo Nænia planctu, Pectora quo concussa fremant interrita quauis, Vt discant iustâ simul ac Deus arserit irâ, Flammea tela pio iaculata repellere cultu.
IOH. POLYANDRI IVNIO-RIS, AD ILLVSTRISS. PRIN-cipem Fridericum IIII. &c. Epigramma.
SCIRE cupin' quis sit Iacomotius iste, querelas Qui tibi Ieremia, Dux FRIDE-RICE, dicat?
Urbis hic est Pastor Geneuensis, ubi armat in hostem Marte vel inuito, quâ valet arte, pios.
Plura rogas? Phœbi, sacræ Pietatis & artes Marte vel inuito, quâ valet arte, fouet.

page.notes: The woodcut initial S is joined to SCIRE. The decorative rule above the title is not transcribed. "Ieremia," may be "Ieremiæ" (the final letter is a ligature and is hard to read). "iãbos" has a tilde that is hard to make out. "Iacomotius" and "cupin'" are as far as I can read them.
